title: Inference poisoning detection and traffic quarantine playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook defines detection logic, alert thresholds, and an operational quarantine procedure for suspected inference poisoning (malicious or accidental prompt/body inputs that cause unsafe, privacy-leaking, or unusually low-quality outputs). The goal is to rapidly isolate affected tenants/requests, preserve forensic evidence, and keep the global fleet healthy while minimizing false-positive disruption.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood hosted inference endpoints and Dedicated control-plane proxies.
- Covers real-time detection (online) and retrospective batch detection (offline drift scans).
- Not a substitute for model-level hardening; complements model-safety guardrails and content filters.

Definitions
- Inference poisoning: request traffic patterns or inputs that cause model outputs to reveal sensitive data, produce instructions for misuse, or systematically degrade quality.
- Quarantine: routing selected traffic to an isolated processing path (no outbound side-effect integration, audit-only) for investigation.

Signals and thresholds (table)
- Signal: "sensitive-sequence-likelihood" (model safety classifier score) — Threshold: >= 0.98 for a single-response OR >= 0.85 for 3+ correlated responses within 5 minutes.
- Signal: "high-token-entropy" (surprising generative output measured by negative log-probability spike) — Threshold: > 6.0 nats/token average over 20 tokens.
- Signal: "structured-leak-patterns" (regex-based PII patterns in output: SSN, AWS keys, private keys) — Threshold: any match.
- Signal: "prompt-replay-match" (incoming prompt matches known exfiltration templates hashed in blacklist) — Threshold: similarity >= 0.9.
- Composite rule: trigger when (sensitive-sequence-likelihood OR structured-leak-patterns) AND (rate of such triggers per tenant > 3 / 10min).

Detection algorithm (online)
1. Per-response safety classifier: run lightweight safety model on final tokens; emit score and tags.
2. Sliding-window correlation: maintain per-tenant counters for matched risk tags with a 10-minute TTL.
3. Anomaly cross-check: verify whether the request came with region/agent mismatches or abnormal metadata (user-agent spike, auth token reuse).
4. Score accumulation: compute a quarantine_score: 0.6*max_safety_score + 0.3*token_entropy_norm + 0.1*metadata_anomaly. Threshold for auto-quarantine: >= 0.88.

Telemetry and observability requirements
- Events emitted: inference.safety_check (producer, tenant_id, request_id, score, tags), inference.quarantine.action (tenant_id, request_ids, action, operator), forensic.snapshot (s3_path, retention_tag).
- SLI to monitor: false_positive_rate_of_quarantine (target < 5% monthly), mean_time_to_quarantine (target < 2m for auto-quarantine).
- Dashboards: quarantine overview, per-tenant trigger heatmap, classifier drift chart (weekly).

Traffic quarantine playbook (operational procedure)
Preconditions: on-call (SRE or Safety) has access to the Quarantine Console and forensic storage.
1. Automatic quarantine (if quarantine_score >= 0.88):
   - Control-plane routes subsequent matching requests for tenant to quarantine path for 30 minutes.
   - Mark requests with header X-Redwood-Quarantine: true and attach root-cause tags.
   - Create forensic snapshot: store prompt, model logits (sampled), response, request metadata to secure bucket with retention=90d, write-only to security audit.
   - Fire alert to #sec-safety and on-call SRE with runbook link.
2. Manual quarantine (operator-led):
   - Use Quarantine Console filter (tenant / tenant_ip / request_id).
   - Click "Isolate tenant" to enable quarantine route for specified tenant scope.
   - Optionally enable "sampling-only" to capture 100% of inputs but still serve original path for 15 minutes to reduce customer impact while collecting evidence.
3. Investigation steps (ordered):
   - Triage: confirm output includes PII or unsafe instructions. Document examples in incident record.
   - Reproduce offline in isolated sandbox with identical model variant and kernel config.
   - If reproduction consistent, escalate to Safety + Model Onboarding: attach forensic snapshot and repro artifacts.
   - If confirmed malicious intent (e.g., crafted exfil template), apply tenant-level throttle: requests/sec <= 1 and require API key rotation.
   - If false positive, remove quarantine immediately and annotate classifier training set.
4. Escalation and customer communication:
   - If investigation indicates data-exfil risk, schedule immediate customer notification within 4 hours and coordinate legal/Security.
   - For verified model bug (not tenant misuse), create rollback/variant pin in the model catalog and initiate canary rollback policy.

Rollbacks and remediation actions
- Variant pin: move tenant to last-known-good variant id with immediate effect, retain telemetry to validate behavior across 24h.
- Model rollback decision matrix:
  - If >20% of tenant's recent requests show sensitive leakage -> immediate rollback and 24h quarantine.
  - If bursts localized and reproducible only with certain prompt patterns -> quarantine + client guidance recommended.

Forensics and evidence preservation
- Always preserve an immutable snapshot (write-once S3 path) when quarantine is triggered. Snapshot schema (example):
  {
    "tenant_id": "T-1234",
    "request_id": "r-8a6f...",
    "timestamp": "2026-02-28T14:22:31Z",
    "prompt": "<redacted>",
    "response": "<redacted>",
    "model_variant": "redwood-gptx-3.2q",
    "safety_score": 0.996,
    "evidence_tags": ["SSN-match", "high-entropy"]
  }
- Access to forensic buckets must be logged and gated by role. Audit trail retention = 365d for security investigations.

SLOs and risk appetite
- Acceptance targets: mean_time_to_quarantine < 2 minutes for auto-quarantine, investigation_ttr (time to initial triage) < 1 hour on business-hours incidents.
- Tolerances: allow up to 5% false quarantines monthly; actions should favor safety over availability for verified sensitive leakage.

Testing and drills
- Quarterly fire-drill: synthesize a safe, non-production prompt that triggers the classifier and verify the end-to-end quarantine path.
- Synthetic workload tests: run batch job that injects known exfil patterns and validate detection recall >= 95% in the simulated traffic.
- Post-drill checklist: verify forensic snapshot integrity, confirm alert routing, update classifier training examples for false positives.

Implementation checklist (technical steps)
- Instrument lightweight safety classifier in the response path (developer: runtime-team).
- Add quarantine_score aggregator (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Create Quarantine Console UI + control-plane toggle (owner: eng-platform).
- Secure forensic storage with restrictive IAM, KMS encryption, and mandatory access logging (owner: security).
- Alerting: integrated with PagerDuty -> #sec-safety Slack channel -> on-call rotation (owner: eng-sre).

CLI examples and internal API
- Quarantine a tenant (operator command):
  redwoodctl quarantine isolate --tenant T-1234 --duration 30m --reason "suspected-exfil"
- Snapshot retrieval (read-only, security role):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-forensics/quarantine/T-1234/r-8a6f... /tmp/ --profile sec-readonly
- Sample alert payload (inferred event):
  {
    "event": "inference.safety_check",
    "tenant_id": "T-1234",
    "request_id": "r-8a6f...",
    "score": 0.994,
    "tags": ["SSN-match", "high-entropy"]
  }

Governance and reviews
- Quarterly model-safety review: product, safety, and runtime teams will review false positives/negatives and adjust classifier thresholds.
- Any quarantine action affecting paying customers must be reviewed by Customer Success within 24h and documented in the incident record.

Appendix: safe-handling guidelines for sample data
- Redact PII where possible before sharing snapshots externally. Use tokenized redaction helpers in the Quarantine Console.
- When reproducing, use model variant clones in a locked sandbox with no external network access.

Owners
- Primary: Eng - Serving Runtime (on-call: runtime-safety rotation)
- Backup: Eng - SRE (on-call: infra-safety rotation)
- Security liaison: Security - Threat Ops

Revision history
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2026-02-12: Added forensic snapshot schema and telemetry events (review: Daniel Kim)
- 2026-03-01: Updated thresholds after Q1 safety drill; set quarantine_score and auto-quarantine policy
